test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts-P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

The United Nations was formed after the Second World War.

P: It was established to prevent future global conflicts.

Q: Over the decades, it has expanded its roles.

R: Now it addresses issues like climate change and human rights.

S: Its peacekeeping missions have played a vital role in conflict zones.

6. Despite criticisms, the UN remains a key international body.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The passage begins with the context of the United Nations being formed after the Second World War and highlights its purpose and contributions.
 
• **Sentence P** is the first in the logical sequence because it introduces the purpose of the UN:
 
 
• "It was established to prevent future global conflicts."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q** follows as it explains the evolution of the UN’s role over the years:
 
 
• "Over the decades, it has expanded its roles."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S** comes next as it highlights the peacekeeping missions, which are one of the key roles of the UN:
 
 
• "Its peacekeeping missions have played a vital role in conflict zones."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R** is the last in the sequence as it mentions the current focus areas of the UN:
 
 
• "Now it addresses issues like climate change and human rights."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQSR**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The United Nations was formed after the Second World War. It was established to prevent future global conflicts. Over the decades, it has expanded its roles. Its peacekeeping missions have played a vital role in conflict zones. Now it addresses issues like climate change and human rights. Despite criticisms, the UN remains a key international body."
